recap.back_html: A function decorated with @pytest.fixture. A test gets its value by naming it as a parameter.
Code before yield is setup. Code after yield is teardown, and it runs even when the test fails.
Only for expensive objects that no test changes. A shared object that a test changes makes results depend on test order.

recap.back_html: A fixture that returns a function building fresh data with defaults, so each test states only what matters.
Put them in conftest.py. Tests in that folder and below use them without an import.

snippets: @pytest.fixture
def respondents() -> pd.DataFrame:
return pd.DataFrame({"respondent_id": ["R1", "R2"], "final_weight": [1.0, 3.0]})
def test_total_weight(respondents: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
assert respondents["final_weight"].sum() == 4.0
@pytest.fixture
def make_respondents():
def make(weights: list[float]) -> pd.DataFrame:
ids = [f"R{i}" for i in range(1, len(weights) + 1)]
return pd.DataFrame({"respondent_id": ids, "final_weight": weights})
return make
lessons.takeaway_html: Fixtures give each test fresh data by default. Share a fixture only when it is expensive and nothing changes it.
lessons.title: Fixtures, shared setup without shared state

Standard error sqrt(p(1 - p) / sims). Allow about four standard errors: 0.931 to 0.969 for 0.95 over 2,000 simulations.
p_value < 0.05 on random data. It fails by chance about one run in twenty.

Register markers under markers = [...] and add --strict-markers to addopts. pytest 9 also offers strict = true.
Whether tests check anything. Mutation testing (mutmut 3.8) changes the code and reports changes no test catches.
Fix the cause: seed, shared state, clock or network. A retry hides it.

snippets: pytest --cov=survey_stats --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=90
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--strict-markers"

lessons.takeaway_html: Measure branch coverage and set a floor, register markers strictly, fix flaky tests at the cause, and remember that coverage says what ran, not what was checked.
